findings.reason: the node runs the named controls as its proof, so a control aimed at the wrong case either blocks the node or leaves the record-key and stage-split guards unshown to fire.
findings.text: s4's done-when says "shows four things" but lists five bullets (the per-section fallback memo case was inserted second without renumbering), and its negative controls still reference the old positions: "leaving the review records out of the record's key fails the second case" names the fallback-memo case (bullet 2), which does not depend on the record key, while the record-key case is bullet 3; "timing `advance_waiting_requests` inside `launch_seconds` fails the fourth case" names the verdict-equivalence arm (bullet 4) instead of the `waits_seconds` arm (bullet 5) — under SPEC exact a worker applying those controls finds them passing and cannot satisfy the done-when as written

findings.reason: the discovery gate is the section's only defence against fixing the wrong path, and it currently makes the node block before it can land either fix, so the citation source for the refused attempt has to name where that refusal actually survives.
findings.text: s22's done-when requires that each of the two attempts "is cited with the run record that shows it: the run's `attempt.json`, `supervisor.json`, `stderr.log` or stream line", but the 22:43:56Z attempt was refused at worktree creation and never launched, so it left no run record: `attempt.json` in the cited run directory reads `{"attempt": 1, "attempt_kind": "dispatch", "attempt_started_at": "2026-11-02T22:45:22Z"}` — one attempt, the successful one — leaving the refusal's only trace in the pointer's `failure`/`failure_attempts` keys and the dispatch call's error text, both of which promotion has since rewritten; by the section's own rule ("If a named path is not one the fixes touch, the node stops and reports blocked") the node blocks on a requirement no record can satisfy
